questions.q: A car moves on a straight highway. Its odometer readings at 10:00 AM, 10:05 AM, 10:10 AM, and 10:15 AM are 1200 km, 1205 km, 1210 km, and 1215 km respectively. Is the car in uniform motion? State the condition for uniform motion.
questions.a: Yes, the car is in uniform motion because it covers equal displacements (5 km) in equal time intervals (5 minutes). The condition for uniform motion is constant velocity: equal displacements in equal intervals of time along a straight line. A wrong answer (e.g., saying speed is constant but not checking direction) reveals the student confuses uniform speed with uniform velocity, ignoring the straight-line requirement.

questions.q: A boy runs around a square track of side 50 m at a constant speed of 5 m/s. Is his motion uniform or non-uniform? Explain why, referencing the definition of velocity.
questions.a: The motion is non-uniform. Although speed is constant (5 m/s), the direction changes at each corner of the square track. Velocity is a vector (magnitude + direction); since direction changes, velocity changes. Uniform motion requires constant velocity. A wrong answer (claiming uniform because speed is constant) reveals the misconception that uniform motion only requires constant speed, neglecting the vector nature of velocity.

questions.q: An object moves along a straight line. Its displacements in successive 3-second intervals are: 6 m, 6 m, 6 m, 9 m, 6 m. Calculate the average velocity for the first 12 seconds and for the total 15 seconds. Is the motion uniform throughout? Justify.
questions.a: First 12 s: total displacement = 6+6+6+6 = 24 m (four intervals of 3 s each). Average velocity = 24 m / 12 s = 2 m/s. Total 15 s: total displacement = 24+9 = 33 m. Average velocity = 33 m / 15 s = 2.2 m/s. Motion is NOT uniform throughout because the displacement in the fourth interval (9 m) differs from the others (6 m), indicating changing velocity. A wrong calculation (e.g., averaging speeds) reveals inability to apply the definition of uniform motion to discrete data.

questions.q: Two distance-time graphs are shown: Graph A is a straight line passing through origin with slope 4 m/s. Graph B is a curve that gets steeper with time. (a) Which graph represents uniform motion? (b) What does the slope of Graph A represent? (c) If Graph B represents a car accelerating from rest, what can you say about its velocity at different times?
questions.a: (a) Graph A represents uniform motion because a straight line on a distance-time graph indicates constant speed (equal distances in equal times). (b) The slope of Graph A represents the speed (magnitude of velocity) of the object, which is 4 m/s. (c) For Graph B, the slope increases with time, meaning the velocity increases with time; the car is accelerating. A wrong answer (e.g., saying Graph B is uniform because it's smooth) reveals inability to interpret graphical slope as velocity.

questions.q: A student claims: "A satellite orbiting Earth at constant speed is in uniform motion because its speed doesn't change." Evaluate this statement and correct it if necessary.
questions.a: The statement is incorrect. Uniform motion requires constant velocity (both magnitude and direction). A satellite in orbit continuously changes direction (towards Earth's center), so its velocity changes even though speed is constant. This is uniform circular motion, which is a type of non-uniform motion. A student who agrees reveals the misconception that constant speed alone defines uniform motion, ignoring the vector nature of velocity and the role of centripetal acceleration.

questions.q: Give the correct order of steps for the toy-car experiment that tests whether motion on a tilted plank is uniform.
questions.a: The procedure runs: (1) Mark positions at 20 cm intervals along the plank (2) Release the car from rest at the top (3) Record the time at which the car passes each mark (4) Compare displacements per equal time interval and conclude uniform motion when they match. A wrong answer that only measures total time shows the student cannot design a test of equal displacements in equal intervals, which is the definition of uniform motion.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Uniform motion is motion in which an object covers equal ______ in equal intervals of time, implying constant velocity (both magnitude and direction remain unchanged).
Fill in the blank: Observe a ceiling fan rotating at constant speed – the blades cover equal angles in equal time but their direction changes ______.
What is Uniform motion? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Uniform motion is motion in which an object covers equal displacements in equal intervals of time, implying constant velocity (both magnitude and direction remain unchanged).

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Now compare with a bicycle moving on a straight road at a steady ______ km/h.
What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Uniform motion?
questions.a: Students often think "uniform motion = constant speed" and classify uniform circular motion as uniform motion.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student can distinguish uniform from non-uniform motion using displacement-time data, velocity-time data, and graphical representations, and can explain why a body moving at constant speed in a circular path is in non-uniform motion.
